accuracy.reason: All eight objectives correctly distinguish routing from replication, capacity creation and business-effect safety. Health sampling/all-unhealthy behavior and connection-aware draining avoid false availability guarantees.

evidence.quote: Check the product's all-unhealthy policy too. Some balancers send traffic to unhealthy targets when every target fails its checks, rather than refusing all traffic.

mechanisms.reason: Reader can trace forward/return proxy path, repeated requests on one connection, selection signals, sampled health removal, local session loss, drain cutoff/deadline and atomic retry protection. Both diagrams show those state boundaries accurately.

evidence.quote: Stopping new L4 connections does not stop new HTTP requests on existing connections. A drain must also manage those connection lifetimes or stop accepting further requests. L7 request-aware draining must still track already accepted work.

coherence.reason: Path and routing unit precede policy, readiness and session placement; planned removal and retry failures build on those actors before whole-path capacity. Every card objective and criterion is supported, with no missing prerequisite.

evidence.quote: Many HTTP requests can reuse that connection. They can all reach the same backend; adding requests on that connection does not force new selections.

decisions.reason: Gives conditional algorithm choices, single-server alternative, affinity/shared-store costs, bounded drain and retry responses, plus surviving capacity and reachable entry requirements. Choices connect actual workload and failure constraints.

evidence.quote: Headroom is spare capacity. After one backend fails, the survivors need enough capacity for the remaining load. Otherwise redirecting traffic can overload them. Limit or reject excess work visibly instead of assuming redistribution solves it.

clarity.reason: Defines backend, L4/L7, readiness, session, affinity, in-flight work, key/deduplication and headroom at use. Examples expose specific errors without jargon accumulation; actual learner quotes exactly support all six transfers.

evidence.quote: A stable ID for one logical operation, reused on every attempt. Deduplication means recognizing a repeat. A new key per retry, or a key remembered only in one server's memory, cannot reliably protect retries elsewhere.

outcomes.reason: All four criteria: learner traces both proxy directions, chooses HTTP-aware L7 with TLS visibility, explains connection-bound L4 reuse, and conditions the extra component on distribution or redundancy needs. Slides 1–2 teach each inference.

All four criteria: distinguishes turns, active connections and configured shares with each limitation; conditionally uses least connections/weights and measurement. Shared database saturation survives extra API capacity; reachable alternate entry and surviving headroom are both explicit.

All four criteria: purchase capability differs from endpoint response; sampled intervals/thresholds and coverage prevent instant certainty. Removal stops new eligible selection, cannot repair in-flight work; learner also preserves the all-unhealthy fail-open exception.

All three criteria: B lacks A-only state and A loss can lose the copy; affinity restricts placement/skews load without replication. Shared storage enables cross-backend access but adds coordination and availability dependency.

All three criteria: stop assignments, manage existing connections and accepted work, then stop at completion or bounded deadline. Learner does not assume the unspecified deadline exceeds 20 seconds or that unfinished work migrates.

All four criteria: unknown committed outcome can duplicate on B; stable operation key and shared durable result are atomically coordinated with effect. New keys/local memory fail recognition, separate checks race, retries consume capacity and need bounds/delay.

sourceChecks.claim: AWS verifies traffic distribution and stable target service role. Supplement https://nginx.org/en/docs/beginners_guide.html verifies reverse-proxy response path. Extra hop/operation cost and single-server alternative are explicit design tradeoffs; diagram correctly selects one backend.

Azure verifies L4 transport versus L7 path routing. Supplement https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/introduction.html specifies one target per TCP lifetime; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/ssl-overview verifies readable decrypted HTTP and separately configured backend TLS.

NGINX verifies round robin, least active connections and weights, including varying request duration and weighted request examples. Counters do not measure arbitrary work and static weights do not promise performance; conditional choices are appropriately limited.

AWS verifies periodic path checks, thresholds, removal and all-unhealthy fail-open. Supplement https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/health-endpoint-monitoring verifies dependency-aware useful-work checks. Sampling cannot rescue already failed operations.

Web-farm source verifies shared state/cache dependencies and errors when requests reach another node. Supplement https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/app-state?view=aspnetcore-10.0 verifies memory-local sessions, sticky scalability costs and distributed storage alternative. Routing does not copy memory.

AWS verifies new-request cutoff, draining interval and interrupted connection errors. TCP lifetime from https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/introduction.html explains existing-connection caveat. Deadline and non-migration warning are correct; diagram explicitly separates accepted A work from new B assignments.

AWS idempotency source checked in r12 verifies same logical token, atomic mutations/token and equivalent repeated response. Durable shared unique reservation plus database effect/result is a concrete scoped implementation. Delayed bounded retries also supported by https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/retry.

Google overload source verifies finite capacity, shedding and retry amplification. Supplement https://sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend/ verifies avoidance of one entry failure point; AWS NLB introduction describes reachable surviving nodes. A shared bottleneck and survivor capacity require whole-path reasoning, as taught.
